note.c: <P_f_Footnote><SP_f_AO_3a_-LIT>Ünal A. 1974b</SP_f_AO_3a_-LIT>, 78 reads <SP_f_AO_3a_SumGRAM>KUR</SP_f_AO_3a_SumGRAM> instead of <SP_f_AO_3a_SumGRAM>PAP</SP_f_AO_3a_SumGRAM>, apparently misunderstanding a marginal note on the passage by the copyist and editor of KUB 5, Arnold Walther “dann KUR darüber”. Yet, as <SP_f_AO_3a_-LIT>Beal R.H. 1999a</SP_f_AO_3a_-LIT>, 51f. note 48 notes, the reading of the sign <SP_f_AO_3a_SIGN>PAP</SP_f_AO_3a_SIGN> in the beginning of the 20th century was different from today’s. Thus, Walther meant that <SP_f_AO_3a_SIGN>PAP</SP_f_AO_3a_SIGN> which can also be read KÚR (or, in the time of the publication KUR) was written over an erased sign. Remarkable is the fact that, in contrast to the normal usage, <SP_f_AO_3a_SumGRAM>PAP</SP_f_AO_3a_SumGRAM> is not written with a phonetic complement (<SP_f_AO_3a_SumGRAM>PAP</SP_f_AO_3a_SumGRAM>-<SP_f_AO_3a_Hittite>nu-mar)</SP_f_AO_3a_Hittite>. In general, also a reading <SP_f_AO_3a_SumGRAM>KÚR</SP_f_AO_3a_SumGRAM> “enemy” is possible which, however, is usually written with the determinative <SP_f_AO_3a_Determ>LÚ</SP_f_AO_3a_Determ>.</P_f_Footnote>
